sents.t: Every spring, Oakville has a Volunteer Day.
People help at schools, parks, and the food bank.
This year, Lily and I signed up to work at the Oakville Food Bank.
On Saturday morning, a volunteer leader named Mrs. Johnson gave us bright orange T-shirts.
“The food bank gives free food to families who need help,” she explained.
“Today, we have to sort and pack two thousand cans and boxes.”
“I’ll carry the heavy boxes,” I said.
“And I’ll sort the cans,” said Lily.
We worked in a big warehouse with about fifty other volunteers.
Some were high school students, and some were retired people.
An old man named Walter told me, “I’ve volunteered here every month for ten years. It’s the best part of my month.”
In the afternoon, families came to pick up food.
A little girl said “Thank you!” and gave Lily a drawing of a sun.
“Will you come again next month?” Mrs. Johnson asked.
